message.content: Lion and zebra share a common ancestor within the order **Carnivora** (for lions) and **Perissodactyla** (for zebras). However, if we look at a broader level, both belong to the class **Mammalia**. Their most recent common ancestor would be a mammalian ancestor that lived tens of millions of years ago, before the divergence of the major mammalian orders. In terms of evolutionary relationships, lions are part of the family Felidae, while zebras belong to the family Equidae. They diverged from a common ancestor that was a more primitive mammal, likely a member of the clade **Euarchontoglires** or **Laurasiatheria**, depending on the phylogenetic hypothesis. The exact common ancestor is not well-defined due to incomplete fossil records and ongoing debates in mammalian phylogeny.
